title: #stitch with @Spencer Glass  always noting that shows are in previews...
transcript: Three is when you see a show in previews, then you come on here and you post a review. Every time we get into this conversation, I feel like there's a nuance that is lost here. I don't disagree with what Spencer is saying, because I think when a show is in previews, it's really important to note in talking about the show that it's in previews and that things change. Think a lot about once upon a one more time. That, like, massively changed in previews, and people were blasting it after, like, two days, and then, like, the show got so much better and so many people didn't see it because they saw, like, videos and reviews saying the show is bad. Maybe you still don't like the show, and that's fine, but, like, it did get significantly better. That being said, many people pay full price tickets to go see shows and previews. Yes, some shows do special preview discounts. We can get, like, balcony seats for a certain price, or they'll have, like, a special lottery for previews. But most shows, they just charge you the same price if you saw it the first day of previews or a week after opening. And most people can't afford to see a show more than once. Kind of think if the expectation is that you go see a show in previews that you're only ever going to see once, and then you can't talk about it because the Show isn't finished, despite the fact that they are. You're paying a price to go see an unfinished product. It's kind of hard to tell people that they can't talk about it. I don't know what the answer is here, other than we all seem to be cognizant of if you want to talk about a show, noting that's in previews, if you go to see a first preview and you're like, here are my thoughts on the first preview, as opposed to being like, here are my thoughts on the show, I definitely think there's a difference between having a constructive conversation or review as opposed to just, like, making content for views, because, you know, the meaner you are, the more views you'll get. I don't know. These are just my thoughts of someone who makes theater content. Although I would not consider myself a reviewer. The way that I'm more consider it is I'm a theater matchmaker. Like, if you like these things, you'll like this show. And I see everything, and I can help you find a show that you would want to see and that you would enjoy. Because that's always my goal, is to get the right people to the right shows and bring the right audiences to the right places. I don't think we can tell people to not speak or share their opinions and thoughts. I think we can tell them to be a little more cognizant and aware and Use the right language when talking about them
